title: zenith-bank-integration-call-notes-2026-03-10
content:
Meeting: Zenith Bank — Redwood integration kickoff (video call)
Date: 2026-03-10
Attendees: Aisha Patel (Redwood SE), Tom Reynolds (Redwood PM), Liu Chen (Redwood SRE),
           Priya Menon (Zenith — Platform), Marco Alvarez (Zenith — ML infra), Samir Rao (Zenith — Sec)

High-level summary:
- Zenith is exploring Redwood Private (VPC) for internal LLM features: conversational support in agent UI + redaction pipeline for PII.
- Primary constraints: strict data residency (EU-only), HSM/KMS integration for keys, enterprise SLA (99.9 uptime), and predictable tail latency (p95 < 300ms for short prompts).
- Pilot scope: onboarding 1 model family (open Llama variant) for a chat assistant and a reranker for search relevance. 1 month pilot, target 1000 concurrent users/day at launch, 10 qps steady-state during business hours.

Notes / requirements (raw):
- Networking: Zenith will run in AWS eu-west-1. They want Redwood Private with customer-managed VPC peering and flow logs forwarded to their SIEM.
- Auth: must support KMS-backed key encryption + HSM for signing. They call out required FIPS compatibility for certs. 
- Data handling: logs must be configurable — redaction required before leaving VPC. They ask for optional token-level cost telemetry but only after PII scrubbed.
- Models: prefer open models (weight pull from internal registry). They want guidance on quantization (8-bit vs 4-bit) and impact on latency/quality.
- Latency: p50 target 80–120ms for <256 tokens, p95 <300ms. Concerned about cold-starts and KV cache warmup.
- Throughput: initial expected 500–800 users/day, burst to 3k/day for marketing events. Need autoscale/backpressure behavior documented.
- Monitoring: require per-route dashboards + tracing to trace requests from app -> Redwood -> model. Want log retention 90d (shorter retention for token traces).
- Security/compliance: SOC2 plus contract clause for data deletion on contract end. They will require audit logs for all model access.

Gotchas / risks called out in conversation:
- Model version pinning: they will insist on pinning exact model + quantization profile. Need clear rollback plan when we update runtime kernels (they worried about subtle output changes).
- KV cache eviction: their chat UX depends on long context; we need to estimate memory for active sessions and eviction policy. If we evict too aggressively, UX degrades.
- Fallbacks: they want automatic fallback to smaller model during regional outage but worry about inconsistent outputs. We suggested labeling fallback model as "graceful-degrade" and surface in UI.
- Billing visibility: Zenith's procurement insists on per-team cost allocation. Must support tagging/route-level meters.

Action items / next steps (owners + ETA):
- Aisha: draft high-level pilot plan (architecture diagram + network flow) and share by 2026-03-12. (IN PROGRESS)
- Tom: prepare SLA + pricing sketch for Dedicated vs Private (commit tiers) — due 2026-03-15. (TODO)
- Liu: run capacity calc for KV cache sizing given 1k concurrent sessions with avg 4k token history — deliver numbers 2026-03-13. (TODO)
- Marco (Zenith): provide expected prompt length distribution and peak concurrency windows (by 2026-03-12).
- Priya (Zenith): internal security questionnaire + comms for KMS/HSM vendor (by 2026-03-14).
- Aisha/Tom: schedule follow-up tech deep-dive for infra team (2 hours) — propose 2026-03-17.

Open questions (for next call):
- Which HSM/KMS vendor will Zenith use? Need contact + example integration docs.
- How strict is p95 <300ms requirement across all routes vs only chat endpoints? Clarify per-route SLOs.
- Are they OK with partial telemetry (aggregate token counts) if token-level traces are restricted?
- Do they require model provenance bios for each model version (training data disclaimers)?

Loose thoughts / scratchpad (Aisha):
- For pilot, recommend start with 8-bit quantized model + warmup workers for expected peak periods; document expected quality delta vs 4-bit in short eval.
- Propose canary rollout: 5% traffic for 48 hours, compare throughput/latency and simple QA prompt set.
- Consider caching strategy: session-pin to worker to maximize KV reuse. Tradeoff: less flexible autoscaling. Might be acceptable for launch.
- Prepare a short appendix on "what changes when we change kernels" for procurement/legal to reduce frictions.

References / links mentioned on call:
- Jira ticket: JIRA-ZEN-3421 (provisioning + pilot scope)
- Confluence: confluence:zenith-integration-playbook (draft)
- Slack thread: #zenith-onboarding (internal)
- Red-Team checklist: github:pr/812 (security notes)

Tone: notes are informal — will turn into a proper pilot brief once we gather prompt distributions and security questionnaire.

Next meeting: schedule tech deep-dive week of 2026-03-15 (target 2026-03-17).

-- End of notes (Aisha)
